To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-07T09:07:00-08:00
Subject: Request: temporary p95 derating during data migration

Hi Ben,

We're planning a cross-region data migration the week of Nov 15 to Nov 18. Expected traffic patterns will spike and we anticipate transient service degradation during a brief cutover window. Can Redwood provide a short, contractual exception to the hosted API p95 commitment for that window (target: allow up to 2x p95 for up to 48 hours) and a clear rollback/rollforward plan so our SREs can coordinate?

Important items for us:
- Exact measurement window definition (how you compute the p95 during the event)
- Start/end criteria and expected notification cadence
- Any credit or remediation language if degradation persists beyond the agreed window

Attaching a one-page migration runbook (see stub) and happy to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Michael O'Rourke
VP Engineering, FinSight
ops@finsight.co

Ben / Marissa,

Draft exception language (high level) I recommend we present to FinSight:

- Temporary Derating: Redwood will adjust the p95 latency commitment for the Hosted API to a temporary threshold of 2x the contracted p95 for up to 48 consecutive hours beginning at the mutually agreed UTC start time. The temporary derating applies only to calls routed to the finSight account's US region endpoints (region: us).

- Measurement Window: During the derating period, p50 and p95 will be measured using the same tokenized request-sampling and aggregation methodology used in the master SLA, but samples will be isolated to the FinSight tenant and the agreed 48h window. We will exclude retry-induced spikes and healthcheck noise per standard exclusion rules (as documented in our measurement playbook).

- Start/End Criteria & Notifications:
  * Start: Derating begins at the agreed UTC timestamp and Redwood will send primary notification to ops@finsight.co and the FinSight escalation list.
  * End: Derating will automatically end after 48 consecutive hours unless both parties sign a rollforward.
  * Progress Updates: Redwood will provide cadence updates at T+2h, T+12h, and on termination.

- Rollforward & Remediation: If FinSight requests extension beyond 48h, Redwood will assess operational impact and may approve a single 24h extension with agreement from both parties. If p95 degradation persists after any approved extension and is attributable to Redwood platform faults (not customer migration traffic), Redwood will provide a pro-rated credit calculated per Section 6.3 of the MSA.

- Evidence Package: Redwood will provide evidence (sampled traces, request histograms) for the derating window on request. Delivery timing: within 2 business days after the event.

Attachments I recommend including in the proposal: slo-derating-proposal-v2.pdf (legal text) and rollforward-checklist.xlsx (ops checklist).

If that language looks good I'll mark up for signature and Ben can send to Michael.

--
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: slo-derating-proposal-v2.pdf (pdf, 3 pages)

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-11-08T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary p95 derating during data migration

Adding technical ops detail so FinSight has clarity on monitoring / mitigations:

- Scope: Derating limited to FinSight's tenant ID and the us region. All other tenants retain standard p50/p95 commitments.
- Autoscaling & Burst Policy: We'll enable a temporary 10% burst pool reserved for FinSight during the window; this is subject to cluster capacity. If cluster capacity limits are hit we will redirect excess traffic to a throttled fallback model (non-blocking responses).
- Prefix/KV Cache: We'll freeze cache eviction policies for the FinSight serving pool for the 48h window to reduce cold-start amplification.
- Canary & Rollforward: We propose a 30-minute canary at T+0 (first 30 minutes) to verify traffic pathing; if error rate > 1% or p95 > 3x after the canary, we will abort and execute rollback steps in rollforward-checklist.xlsx.
- Monitoring hooks: We'll provide a shared dashboard and an alert channel in the FinSight Ops Slack (read-only post-event).

I'll own the run-of-show and will be on-call for the event. Attaching an ops checklist draft.

Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: rollforward-checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 6 sheets)

Michael — thanks for the patience. Attached is Redwood's formal exception proposal combining Lauren's legal language and Marissa's ops checklist. Key points summarized below:

- Window: Nov 15 00:00 UTC to Nov 17 23:59 UTC (48 consecutive hours) — subject to your confirmation.
- Derating: p95 may be allowed up to 2x contracted p95 for FinSight tenant in US region for that window. p50 remains unchanged.
- Canary: 30-minute canary at start; abort criteria: >1% error or p95 > 3x after canary.
- Evidence & Credits: If persistent degradation beyond approved window is attributable to Redwood, pro-rated credit will apply per MSA; evidence delivered within 2 business days.
- Follow-up: Please confirm the UTC start timestamp and share expected peak RPS. Once confirmed we'll send a DocuSign addendum for signature.

Next steps: reply with "CONFIRM" + UTC start and expected peak RPS and we'll issue the addendum.

Best,
